chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, said: I took a copy of the letter of al-Mutawakkil to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام from Yahya ibn Harthamah in the year two hundred and forty-three, and this is its copy.

In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. To proceed: the Commander of the Faithful recognizes your worth, observes your kinship, and deems your right obligatory. He considers, regarding you and the people of your household, such matters by which Allah may rectify your condition and theirs, confirm your honor and their honor, and bring blessing and security upon you and upon them, seeking thereby the pleasure of his Lord and the fulfillment of what has been made obligatory upon him concerning you and concerning them.

And the Commander of the Faithful has seen fit to remove Abdullah ibn Muhammad from what he had been overseeing of war and salat (prayer) in the city of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, since he was as you mentioned regarding his ignorance of your right and his belittling of your worth, and because of what he imputed to you and ascribed to you of the matter from which the Commander of the Faithful knows your innocence, and the truthfulness of your intention in refraining from pursuing it, and that you did not put yourself forward for it.

And the Commander of the Faithful has appointed over that Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, and ordered him to honor you, revere you, comply with your command and your view, and seek nearness to Allah and to the Commander of the Faithful through that. And the Commander of the Faithful longs for you and loves to renew acquaintance with you and to look upon you. So if you are inclined to visit him and remain in his presence for whatever duration you see fit, then you may set out, together with whomever you wish from your household, your mawali, and your attendants, in ease and tranquility, departing when you wish, halting when you wish, and traveling however you wish.

And if you would like Yahya ibn Harthamah, the mawla of the Commander of the Faithful, and those with him from the troops, to accompany you, departing with your departure and traveling with your travel, then the decision in that is left to you until you arrive before the Commander of the Faithful.

For there is no one among his brothers, his children, the people of his household, and his close associates who holds a more gracious position with him, nor for whom his preference is more praiseworthy; nor is he more considerate toward them, more compassionate toward them, more dutiful with them, or more reassuring to them, than he is toward you, if Allah the Exalted wills. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings. Written by Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family and grant peace.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the ruling caliph, referred to here in official court language
key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ: the Imam’s household and family members
key_terms.بَرَاءَتَكَ: your innocence and disavowal from the accusation
key_terms.تَبْجِيلِكَ: showing you reverence and exalted respect
key_terms.جَهَالَتِهِ: his ignorance, referring to Abdullah ibn Muhammad’s lack of recognition of the Imam’s right
key_terms.مَوَالِيكَ: your close associates or dependents attached to your household
key_terms.مُشَيِّعِينَ: those accompanying and escorting you on the journey

ai.seo_question: What does al-Mutawakkil’s letter to Imam al-Hadi عليه السلام say about his summons from al-Madinah?
ai.summary: This report preserves the text of al-Mutawakkil’s letter to Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام, inviting him from al-Madinah and presenting the move as an act of honor and concern. It is historically significant for documenting the political circumstances surrounding the Imam’s summons and the official language used toward Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions who said, 
‘I took a copy of the letter of Al-Mutawakkil to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3<sup>rd</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), from Yahya Bin Harsama, in the year two hundred and forty three, and this here is its copy: -

In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Beneficent, the Merciful. As for afterwards – It is so that the commander of the faithful (the Caliph himself), recognises your<sup>asws</sup> worth, looking after you<sup>asws</sup> due to your<sup>asws</sup> near relationship Obligated for your<sup>asws</sup> right. He is able from the affairs regarding you<sup>asws</sup> and regarding the people of your<sup>asws</sup> household, what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Correct your<sup>asws</sup> state with and their state, and affirms your<sup>asws</sup> honour by it and their honour, and the security upon you<sup>asws</sup> and upon them. He (the Caliph himself) is seeking the Pleasure of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup> by that, and fulfil whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> Necessitated upon him regarding you<sup>asws</sup> and regarding them.

And the commander of the faithful views that he should change Abdullah Bin Muhammad from what he had made him the commander of the forces and the (leader) of the Salat at the city of Rasool-Allahsaww, when it was upon what youasws mentioned from his ignorance of yourasws rights and his belittling yourasws worth, and during what he accused with and linked to youasws from the matters which the commander of the faithful knows of yourasws disavowing from it, and ratifies yourasws intentions regarding the neglect of his attempts, and youasws yourselfasws were not rightful for it.

And the commander of the faithful has hereby had made to rule, what he had ruled from that, Muhammad Bin Al-Fazl and ordered him with honouring you<sup>asws</sup> and revering you<sup>asws</sup> and the ending up to your<sup>asws</sup> orders and your<sup>asws</sup> view, and to get closer to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and to the commander of the faithful by that. And the commander of the faithful is desirous to you<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> would love to renew the covenant with you<sup>asws</sup> and look at you<sup>asws</sup>. So if you<sup>asws</sup> were to activate for visiting him and the staying before him for as long as you<sup>asws</sup> see fit, yourself and the ones you<sup>asws</sup> love from your<sup>asws</sup> family, and your<sup>asws</sup> friends, and your<sup>asws</sup> attendants upon a deadlines and suitability of riding whenever you<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, and lodge whenever you<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, and travel however you<sup>asws</sup> so desire to.

And if you<sup>asws</sup> so like that there should happen to be Yahya Bin Harsama, a slave of the commander of the faithful, and the ones with him from the forces to be walking for you<sup>asws</sup>, riding with your<sup>asws</sup> rides and travelling with your<sup>asws</sup> travels, the command regarding that is to you<sup>asws</sup> until you arrive to the commander of the faithful.

So there is no one from his brethren, and his children, and his family members, and his special ones he would be kinder to in status, nor praiseworthy to of effects, nor is he more considerate to them and more merciful upon them and more righteous with them, or peaceful to him than he would be to youasws, if Allahazwj the Exalted so Desires. And the greetings be upon youasws and the Mercy of Allahazwj and Hisazwj Blessings. And written by Ibrahim Bin Al-Abbas (a scribe), and may Allahazwj Send Salawat upon Muhammadsaww and hissaww Progenyasws, and greetings’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from a man from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who has said the following.

“Abu ya‘qub informed me saying, ‘ I saw him (Muhammad) before his death in the army camp in an evening. Abu al-Hassan received him and looked at him and he became ill the next day. After several days I went to visit him during his illness and his illness was worsening. He informed me that he (abu al-Hassan (a.s.) has sent him cloths which he had folded to use as a pillow. The narrator has said that he was shrouded in that cloth.”

Ahmad has said that abu ya‘qub said, “I saw abu al-Hassan (a.s.) with ibn al-Khadib who said to him, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, go ahead.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “You go first.”
Only after four days he was put in shackles and the news of his death was given out.

The narrator has said that it is narrated that when ibn al-Khadib insisted in his demand from him the house he sent him this messages. “I will ask Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, to place as such that not even your traces would be found.”
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, took him away in those days.”
